use.how: A predicate after a topic like 重要性, 意义, 好处 or 用意: 其中的道理不言而喻。 Says that a meaning or value needs no explaining.

near.diff: 显而易见 says a fact or conclusion is easy to see from the evidence; 不言而喻 says a meaning, value or feeling needs no words.

cue: An article says that clean water matters to everyone's health, and adds that nobody needs to be told why. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 健康的重要性{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: The importance of health goes without saying.

ctx.s: 父母对孩子的爱是{不言而喻}的。
ctx.en: Parents' love for their children goes without saying.

ctx.s: 这次合作对两家公司的意义{不言而喻}，双方都非常重视。
ctx.en: What this partnership means to both companies goes without saying; both sides take it very seriously.

ctx.s: 老板没有明说，但他的意思{不言而喻}：再出错就得走人。
ctx.en: The boss didn't spell it out, but his meaning was clear without words: one more mistake and you're out.

ctx.s: 两人相视一笑，彼此的默契{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: The two of them exchanged a smile; the understanding between them needed no words.

ctx.s: 这条围巾是她亲手织的，其中的心意{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: She knitted this scarf herself; the feeling behind it needs no words.

bad.s: 他{不言而喻}地离开了房间。
bad.en: (meant: he left the room without a word)
bad.why: It is said of a meaning that needs no explaining, not of a person staying silent; for leaving without a word say yì shēng bù kēng.

bad.s: 我对这件事{不言而喻}，所以没发表意见。
bad.en: (meant: I had nothing to say about it, so I kept quiet)
bad.why: Its subject is the point or value that is self-evident, never the person who keeps quiet.

use.how: A predicate or attributive about a fact, difference or conclusion (结论显而易见), or at the head of a sentence: 显而易见，他没准备。

near.diff: 不言而喻 stresses that something need not be said; 显而易见 stresses that anyone looking at the evidence can see it.

cue: The sales chart shows one product's line shooting up and the other's flat. Anyone looking can tell which one wins. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 这个错误{显而易见}，你怎么没发现？
ctx.en: This mistake is plain to see; how did you miss it?

ctx.s: {显而易见}，他没有认真准备这次面试。
ctx.en: Obviously, he didn't prepare properly for this interview.

ctx.s: 数据摆在这里，结论{显而易见}：新方案效果更好。
ctx.en: The data is right here and the conclusion is obvious: the new plan works better.

ctx.s: 两种手机的差别{显而易见}，一个比另一个轻得多。
ctx.en: The difference between the two phones is obvious: one is much lighter than the other.

ctx.s: 医生看了片子说，骨折{显而易见}，需要马上手术。
ctx.en: The doctor looked at the X-ray and said the fracture was plain to see and needed surgery right away.

ctx.s: 城市扩张带来的交通问题已经{显而易见}了。
ctx.en: The traffic problems caused by the city's expansion are now obvious to everyone.

bad.s: 她长得{显而易见}，大家都注意到她了。
bad.en: (meant: she is striking to look at, everyone noticed her)
bad.why: It says a fact or conclusion is obvious, not that a person stands out; for a striking person use yǐn rén zhù mù.

bad.s: 他{显而易见}地告诉我真相。
bad.en: (meant: he told me the truth clearly)
bad.why: It describes facts being obvious, not a clear way of speaking; say he told me míngmíng báibái (plainly).

mean: (formal) beyond dispute, leaving no room to question it
lit: there is no need to cast any doubt on it

use.how: A predicate about a fact, claim or quality (他的能力毋庸置疑), or at the head of a sentence. Used to assert something firmly in speeches, reports and essays.

near.diff: 显而易见 says a thing is easy to see; 毋庸置疑 asserts that it cannot be doubted, and sounds more formal and authoritative.

cue: A spokesperson insists that the company's commitment to safety is so firm that nobody can question it. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 他的专业能力{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: His professional ability is beyond question.

ctx.s: 这份报告的数据来源可靠，结论{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: The report's data comes from reliable sources; its conclusions are beyond dispute.

ctx.s: {毋庸置疑}，科技正在改变我们的生活方式。
ctx.en: There is no doubt that technology is changing the way we live.

ctx.s: 发言人表示，公司对产品质量的承诺是{毋庸置疑}的。
ctx.en: The spokesperson said the company's commitment to product quality is beyond question.

ctx.s: 尽管他有不少缺点，但他对球队的贡献{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: Despite his many flaws, his contribution to the team is beyond dispute.

ctx.s: 记者问判断会不会出错，专家回答：证据确凿，{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: A reporter asked whether the judgement could be wrong; the expert replied: the evidence is conclusive, there is no room for doubt.

bad.s: 妈妈，我{毋庸置疑}想吃冰淇淋！
bad.en: (meant: Mum, I really want ice cream!)
bad.why: It is a formal assertion about facts or claims, not a way to stress a personal wish in casual talk; just say tèbié xiǎng.

bad.s: 我对他的话{毋庸置疑}。
bad.en: (meant: I don't doubt what he says at all)
bad.why: It describes the claim itself, not a person's attitude; to say you fully believe someone use shēn xìn bù yí.

mean: not open to serious criticism, understandable
lit: nothing that may be heavily faulted

use.how: A predicate about a motive or action, often followed by a reservation: 追求利润本无可厚非，但要守法。 A mild defence, not praise.

near.diff: 情有可原 excuses a wrong already done because of the circumstances; 无可厚非 says the action or motive itself is not really wrong.

cue: Your friend wants a better-paid job. You think that's a perfectly fair wish, but you add that she shouldn't lie on her CV. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 想多赚点钱，这{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Wanting to earn a bit more money is perfectly understandable.

ctx.s: 年轻人追求时尚本来{无可厚非}，但不能超出自己的能力。
ctx.en: There's nothing wrong with young people following fashion, but they shouldn't spend beyond their means.

ctx.s: 他第一次上台，紧张一点{无可厚非}，但总该把台词背熟吧。
ctx.en: It was his first time on stage, so being a bit nervous is understandable, but he should at least have learned his lines.

ctx.s: 商家为了吸引顾客打折促销，本身{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Shops offering discounts to attract customers is not something to criticise in itself.

ctx.s: 问：她拒绝加班有错吗？答：合同里没写，她拒绝也{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Q: Was she wrong to refuse overtime? A: It isn't in her contract, so you can hardly blame her.

ctx.s: 评论员写道，球队换帅的决定{无可厚非}，问题出在时机上。
ctx.en: The commentator wrote that the decision to change coaches was defensible; the problem was the timing.

bad.s: 他的画画得{无可厚非}，真是天才！
bad.en: (meant: his painting is flawless, he's a genius!)
bad.why: It only says something is not blameworthy, a mild defence; for faultless work use wú kě tiāo tì.

bad.s: 我们要{无可厚非}地批评他。
bad.en: (meant: we must criticise him severely)
bad.why: It does not mean severely; it is a predicate judging an action excusable, the opposite of harsh criticism.

use.how: A predicate about a person facing pleas, suffering or emotion: 他却无动于衷。 Usually reproaches coldness or stubborn indifference.

near.diff: 漠不关心 is a general lack of concern; 无动于衷 is failing to react to a specific appeal, sight or event that should move one.

cue: A child is crying in front of her father and pleading with him, and he just keeps reading his newspaper. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 孩子哭了半天，他却{无动于衷}。
ctx.en: The child cried for ages, but he remained completely unmoved.

ctx.s: 看到这么感人的电影，你怎么能{无动于衷}？
ctx.en: How can you watch such a moving film and feel nothing?

ctx.s: 不管我怎么劝，他都{无动于衷}，坚持要辞职。
ctx.en: No matter how I tried to talk him round, he wouldn't budge and insisted on quitting.

ctx.s: 面对员工的抱怨，管理层始终{无动于衷}。
ctx.en: Faced with the staff's complaints, management showed no reaction at all.

ctx.s: 老人摔倒了，旁边几个人却{无动于衷}，这让大家很气愤。
ctx.en: An old man fell, yet the people next to him did nothing, which made everyone angry.

ctx.s: 她把信读了两遍，仍然{无动于衷}，随手放进了抽屉。
ctx.en: She read the letter twice, still unmoved, and tossed it into the drawer.

bad.s: 这台机器坏了，按什么按钮都{无动于衷}。
bad.en: (meant: the machine is broken, it doesn't respond to any button)
bad.why: It describes a person's heart not being moved, not a machine that fails to respond; say méiyǒu fǎnyìng.

bad.s: 他遇到危险时{无动于衷}，真勇敢！
bad.en: (meant: he stayed calm in danger, how brave!)
bad.why: It reproaches coldness and is never praise for calm courage; for that use miàn bù gǎi sè.

mean: caring for someone in every little detail
lit: no detail so small that it is not reached

use.how: Modifies care for people: 无微不至地照顾, 无微不至的关怀, 照顾得无微不至. Warm praise of devoted attention.

near.diff: 一丝不苟 is meticulousness in doing a task; 无微不至 is attentive, loving care for a person.

cue: While you were ill, your grandmother cooked your favourite soup, checked your temperature at night and even warmed your slippers. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 妈妈对我的照顾{无微不至}。
ctx.en: My mother looks after me in every little way.

ctx.s: 住院期间，护士们{无微不至}地照顾他。
ctx.en: While he was in hospital, the nurses cared for him attentively in every detail.

ctx.s: 他对女朋友关心得{无微不至}，连她怕冷都记着。
ctx.en: He looks after his girlfriend so attentively that he even remembers she feels the cold.

ctx.s: 这家酒店的服务真是{无微不至}，连雨伞都提前准备好了。
ctx.en: This hotel's service is so attentive that they even had umbrellas ready in advance.

ctx.s: 你别看他平时话不多，对老人的照顾可是{无微不至}。
ctx.en: He may not say much, but the way he looks after the old folks is attentive in every detail.

ctx.s: 感谢信里写道：感谢老师三年来{无微不至}的关怀。
ctx.en: The thank-you letter read: thank you, teacher, for three years of caring for us in every way.

bad.s: 他打扫房间{无微不至}，连角落都擦干净了。
bad.en: (meant: he cleaned the room thoroughly, even the corners)
bad.why: It is about caring for people, not thoroughness in a chore; for careful cleaning use yì sī bù gǒu.

bad.s: 老板对员工的监视{无微不至}，大家都很不满。
bad.en: (meant: the boss watches staff in every detail, and everyone resents it)
bad.why: It is warm praise for loving care and cannot describe surveillance or control.

mean: of no use, not helping at all
lit: of no help to the matter

use.how: A predicate about an action or measure that fails to help: 后悔也无济于事。 It takes no object; say 对……无济于事.

near.diff: 杯水车薪 says the help is far too small for the need; 无济于事 says it does no good at all, for any reason.

cue: You missed the last train home. Standing on the platform shouting at the empty tracks will change nothing. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 现在后悔也{无济于事}了。
ctx.en: Regretting it now won't do any good.

ctx.s: 光着急是{无济于事}的，得想办法。
ctx.en: Just worrying gets us nowhere; we need to find a solution.

ctx.s: 他吃了好几种药，可都{无济于事}。
ctx.en: He took several kinds of medicine, but none of them helped.

ctx.s: 问：要不要再给他打个电话？答：他已经决定了，打了也{无济于事}。
ctx.en: Q: Should I call him again? A: He's made up his mind; calling won't help.

ctx.s: 她又是道歉又是解释，却{无济于事}，客户还是取消了订单。
ctx.en: She apologised and explained, but it was no use; the client still cancelled the order.

ctx.s: 报道指出，临时修补{无济于事}，大桥必须彻底重建。
ctx.en: The report pointed out that temporary repairs are useless; the bridge must be completely rebuilt.

bad.s: 这个人{无济于事}，什么都不会。
bad.en: (meant: this person is useless, he can't do anything)
bad.why: It is said of an action or measure that fails to help, not of a useless person; just say méiyòng.

bad.s: 这些药{无济于事}我的病。
bad.en: (meant: this medicine didn't help my illness)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; put the matter before it with duì, as in: for my illness, the medicine was of no use.

mean: to fabricate something out of nothing
lit: to produce something out of nothing

story.text: The phrase echoes the Daodejing, which says that all things are born of being, and being is born of non-being. It is also the name of the seventh of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, a collection of military ruses: create the appearance of something that is not there in order to deceive the enemy. In everyday speech only the sense of making things up survives.

use.how: A predicate or attributive about rumours, accusations and reports: 纯属无中生有, 无中生有的传言. Accuses someone of inventing claims.

near.diff: 捕风捉影 builds a claim on flimsy hints; 无中生有 invents it with no basis whatsoever.

cue: A newspaper reports that you quarrelled with your boss at a meeting, but you were on holiday that whole week and nothing of the kind happened. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 我根本没说过这种话，你别{无中生有}！
ctx.en: I never said anything like that; don't make things up!

ctx.s: 这篇报道完全是{无中生有}，记者根本没去现场。
ctx.en: This report is pure fabrication; the reporter never even went to the scene.

ctx.s: 有人在网上{无中生有}，说这家餐厅用过期食品。
ctx.en: Someone online invented a story that this restaurant uses expired food.

ctx.s: 问：他说你拿了公司的钱，是真的吗？答：纯属{无中生有}！
ctx.en: Q: He says you took company money; is it true? A: It's a complete fabrication!

ctx.s: 律师警告说，{无中生有}地损害他人名誉要承担法律责任。
ctx.en: The lawyer warned that damaging someone's reputation with fabricated claims carries legal liability.

ctx.s: 老同事们都了解她，那些{无中生有}的传言很快就没人信了。
ctx.en: Her old colleagues knew her well, and soon nobody believed those made-up rumours.

bad.s: 这个地方{无中生有}，什么都没有。
bad.en: (meant: this place is empty, there's nothing here)
bad.why: It does not mean empty; it means inventing claims or stories that have no basis.

bad.s: 我做了个梦，梦里的事都是{无中生有}的。
bad.en: (meant: the things in my dream weren't real)
bad.why: It accuses someone of deliberately inventing claims; a dream is simply unreal, so say it was not true.

mean: so ashamed one wishes the ground would swallow one
lit: no ground in which to hide oneself

use.how: A predicate or complement of feeling: 羞得无地自容, 让我无地自容. Describes intense shame or embarrassment, usually one's own.

near.diff: 面红耳赤 describes a red face from shame, anger or effort; 无地自容 is the inner feeling of wanting to disappear from shame.

cue: Your teacher reads your plagiarised essay aloud next to the original, in front of the whole class. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 被老师当众批评，他羞得{无地自容}。
ctx.en: Criticised by the teacher in front of everyone, he wished the ground would swallow him up.

ctx.s: 想起当年说过的那些傻话，我就{无地自容}。
ctx.en: When I think of the silly things I said back then, I want to sink into the floor.

ctx.s: 她发现自己错怪了朋友，惭愧得{无地自容}。
ctx.en: When she realised she had wrongly blamed her friend, she was overwhelmed with shame.

ctx.s: 问：上台忘词是什么感觉？答：台下几百人看着，我简直{无地自容}。
ctx.en: Q: What's it like to forget your lines on stage? A: Hundreds of people watching; I just wanted to disappear.

ctx.s: 谎言被揭穿的那一刻，他{无地自容}，低着头一句话也说不出来。
ctx.en: The moment his lie was exposed, he was mortified; he hung his head and couldn't say a word.

ctx.s: 父亲的一番话让我{无地自容}：原来他早就知道我逃课了。
ctx.en: What my father said left me mortified: he had known all along that I was skipping class.

bad.s: 房子太小了，我们一家人{无地自容}。
bad.en: (meant: the flat is so small our family has no room)
bad.why: It is about shame, not a lack of physical space; for a flat too small to live in say zhù bú xià.

bad.s: 他做了坏事还{无地自容}，一点也不害羞。
bad.en: (meant: he did wrong and was shameless about it)
bad.why: It means overwhelming shame, the opposite of shamelessness; for shameless use tián bù zhī chǐ.

use.how: After a purpose clause (为了……不择手段) or as an adverbial: 不择手段地打压对手. Always condemns using unscrupulous means to reach a goal.

near.diff: 千方百计 is trying every possible way and can be neutral or praise; 不择手段 condemns using unethical means.

cue: To win the promotion, a manager spread lies about his rival and stole her ideas. Which idiom describes how he went about it?

ctx.s: 为了赚钱，他{不择手段}。
ctx.en: He'll do anything, fair or foul, to make money.

ctx.s: 有些商家{不择手段}地欺骗顾客。
ctx.en: Some businesses will use any trick to cheat their customers.

ctx.s: 为了当上经理，她{不择手段}，连好朋友都出卖了。
ctx.en: To become manager she stopped at nothing, even betraying her best friend.

ctx.s: 为了赢一场比赛就{不择手段}，值得吗？
ctx.en: Is it worth stooping to anything just to win one match?

ctx.s: 我们想成功，但绝不能{不择手段}。
ctx.en: We want to succeed, but never by unscrupulous means.

ctx.s: 电影里的反派是个{不择手段}的人，什么坏事都干得出来。
ctx.en: The villain in the film is utterly unscrupulous, capable of any wicked deed.

bad.s: 他学习{不择手段}，什么方法都试过，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: he tried every study method and finally got into university)
bad.why: It always condemns immoral means; for trying every way to succeed use qiān fāng bǎi jì.

bad.s: 她买衣服{不择手段}，随便拿一件就走。
bad.en: (meant: she isn't picky when buying clothes, she grabs anything)
bad.why: It is not about being unfussy in choosing things; it means using any unscrupulous means to reach a goal.
